name: Bulgarian Split Squat
summary: A single-leg squat with the rear foot elevated on a bench. It heavily loads the front leg's quads and glutes and challenges balance and hip mobility.
setup: Stand about two feet in front of a bench and place the top of one foot on it behind you.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Set your front foot far enough forward that your front shin stays roughly vertical at the bottom.
Brace your trunk with your torso slightly leaning forward.
execution: Lower your hips straight down by bending the front knee.
Keep your front knee tracking in line with your toes and your front foot flat.
Descend until your front thigh is about parallel or as deep as you can control.
Drive through the front foot to stand back up.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.
mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench so the knee runs over the toes and the heel lifts: step the front foot farther forward.
Pushing off the back foot: keep the back leg as a support and drive with the front.
Torso collapsing or swaying: slow down, lighten the load, and brace.
Knee caving in: push it out in line with the toes.
